sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Study both examples. The second one drops some of the wording of the first.

items.prompt: Row 1 has 12 yes and 8 no. Fraction of row 1 saying yes?
For ŷ = 4x + 60, interpret the slope where x is hours studied.

steps: Slope is change in y per unit x.
One more hour is associated with about 4 more points.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Towns with more fire engines report more fire damage. What conclusion is justified?
choices: A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.
Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.
Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.
A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.

items.prompt: A data set records 12, 12, 7, 3, 4. Give the mean and the median.
choices: mean 7.6, median 8
mean 8, median 7
mean 7, median 7.6
mean 7.6, median 7

items.prompt: A data set of five values between 10 and 30 has one additional reading of 244 appended. Which statement best describes the effect on the mean and the median?
choices: The median rises sharply while the mean changes little.
The mean rises sharply while the median changes little, because the mean uses every value’s size.
Neither statistic changes, because one value cannot affect a summary.
Both the mean and the median rise sharply.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 9 yes, 19 no; row 2: 25 yes, 30 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?
A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 9x + 43, where x is measured in hour studieds and y in test points. Interpret the slope.
choices: Each additional test points is associated with 9 more hour studieds.
Each additional hour studied is associated with an increase of about 9 test points.
Each additional hour studied causes an increase of exactly 9 test points.
The predicted value is 9 test points when x is 0.

items.prompt: Ice cream sales and swimming-pool admissions are strongly positively correlated across a year. What conclusion is justified?
choices: Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.
A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.
Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.
A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.

items.prompt: A data set records 13, 29, 9, 5, 7, 19, 9. Give the mean and the median.
choices: mean 13, median 9
mean 13, median 5
mean 13, median 13
mean 9, median 13
